_comment: SYNTHETIC. Every string here was written for this fixture.
It reproduces the STRUCTURE of a real Groundwork decision record -- including
the awkward parts -- so the contract is graded against what records actually
look like rather than against a tidy example. No real project record ships in
this repository: records hold unshipped strategy and private conversation, and
Groundwork is published. The real record's shape is carried, content-free, in
The edge cases it deliberately exercises:
- a prose `status` beginning 'open' on an item that is already ruled
- a ruling of `false`, which is an answer and not an absence
- a whitespace-only ruling, which is a CLEARED ruling and reopens the item
- `ruledAt` with no ruling, which must not close the lane
- an `addressed` axis, settled elsewhere and never ruled
- a preview mapping for text, hide and page modes
- unknown top-level keys a project invented
- an archived annotation with a receipt, and a declined one with a reason

axes.title: How the settings list is grouped
axes.decision: Choose how related settings are visually grouped.
axes.why: Rows currently carry their own borders, so eight settings read as eight unrelated boxes rather than three groups. Grouping is the first thing a person uses to find a setting.
axes.impact: Changes every row on the settings screen.
evidence: Five of six testers scanned the whole list before acting.

options.label: One border per group, dividers between rows
options.cost: Needs a grouping decision for every new setting.

options.label: A border on each row
options.body: Every row is its own card.

axes.title: When a change is written
axes.decision: Choose when an edit reaches the file.
axes.why: Autosaving a destructive setting and autosaving a note are not the same risk.
axes.impact: Changes the save affordance on every control.
axes.note: Notes should not need a button. Anything destructive should.

axes.title: The old navigation bar
axes.decision: Not open — removed before this record was written.

openItems.status: open — pick the current text, the proposal, or write your own
openItems.question: What should the settings heading say?
openItems.why: The current heading names the system, not the task.

openItems.question: Should deleting an account ask twice?
openItems.why: One tap currently removes everything, with no way back.
openItems.whyItMatters: The action is irreversible and the control sits next to a benign one.
openItems.rulingText: Ask twice, and make the second one type the project name.

openItems.question: Keep the advanced options visible by default?
openItems.why: Nine of eleven options are never touched.

openItems.question: What does the reset button say?
openItems.why: The label promises less than the action does.

openItems.question: Should settings move to their own page?
openItems.why: The modal cannot show the advanced group without scrolling twice.

choices.label: Move it to its own page

annotations.note: This heading is doing two jobs at once.

annotations.declinedReason: Red on this background falls below the contrast floor; the surface uses weight and position instead.

history.note: The groups are hard to tell apart.

receipt.what: Replaced per-row borders with one container and inset dividers
receipt.measured: three groups now read as three
